subject: Human Body
title: Parkinson's Disease
description: A micro-lesson that makes Parkinson's Disease usable.

hook.text: Muhammad Ali's hands trembled from Parkinson's. The disease kills dopamine cells that control smooth movement.

buildup.text: Dopamine neurons in the substantia nigra die gradually. By the time tremors appear, 60 to 80% are already gone.

discovery.text: Without dopamine, movements become slow, rigid, and shaky. Simple tasks like buttoning a shirt become exhausting.

twist.text: Levodopa, a dopamine precursor, restores movement temporarily. But it doesn't stop the underlying neuron death.

climax.text: Deep brain stimulation implants an electrode that delivers pulses to motor circuits. It reduces tremors dramatically.

punchline.text: Dopamine cells die silently. Tremors only tell you too late.

quiz.question: What percentage of dopamine neurons are typically gone before symptoms appear?
